variants.name: structured_json
variants.prompt_suffix: Return exactly one JSON object and no other text. Use this schema: {"evidence":["table field and year"],"formula":"numeric arithmetic formula","value":0,"unit":"million|percent|dollars|shares|times|multiple|mmboe|"}. Preserve the table column, row, year, and unit in evidence. Use times or multiple for a ratio, and mmboe when the table uses that unit. The value must be the final answer.

variants.name: evidence_operation
variants.prompt_suffix: Return exactly one JSON object and no other text. Do not output a final value or explanation. Every table cell is labeled [cell_id=rNcM]. Use this schema: {"evidence":[{"cell_id":"r1c2","value":"exact cell value"}],"operands":[0,0],"operation":"subtract","unit":"million|percent|dollars|shares|times|multiple|mmboe|"}. Evidence must use existing cell IDs and copy the exact cell value. Every operand must be copied from a numeric evidence cell, in calculation order. subtract, divide, ratio, percent_change, and absolute_difference require exactly two operands; add and multiply require at least two. For percent_change use [new, old] and unit percent. For ratio use unit times or multiple; use mmboe when the table uses that unit. operation must be one of add, subtract, absolute_difference, multiply, divide, average, ratio, percent_change. The program calculates the final answer deterministically.

variants.name: deterministic_cell_ids_operation
variants.prompt_suffix: Return exactly one JSON object and no other text. The program, not you, performs all arithmetic. Use this schema only: {"cell_ids":["r1c2","r1c3"],"operation":"divide","unit":"percent"}. Return only existing numeric cell IDs in calculation order; do not copy their values, write a formula, or write an answer. Choose operation from add, subtract, multiply, divide, average, ratio, or percent_change. For a percentage of a total use divide with [part, total] and unit percent. For a percentage increase/decrease or growth rate use percent_change with [new, old] and unit percent. For a ratio or multiple use ratio with [numerator, denominator] and unit times. For an average select every requested period and use average. For annual or yearly interest expense select principal and rate cells and use multiply; percent-formatted rate cells are converted to fractions by the program. For a multi-step sum or product, select every numeric input needed and use add or multiply. The program validates cell IDs and computes the result deterministically.

variants.name: deterministic_steps_operation
variants.prompt_suffix: Return exactly one JSON object and no other text. The program performs all arithmetic. Use only this schema: {"steps":[{"operation":"subtract","operands":["r1c2","r1c3"]},{"operation":"divide","operands":["step0","r2c3"]}],"unit":"percent"}. Each operand must be an existing numeric cell ID such as r1c2, a prior result such as step0, or a numeric constant such as 3 when the question explicitly requires it. Steps execute in order. Use divide [part,total] for a percentage of a total, percent_change [new,old] for growth/increase/decrease, average over every requested period, multiply for principal times rate interest expense, and add/subtract for multi-step totals or changes. Do not multiply a percent_change result by 100; the program keeps percentage results as fractions. Do not copy table values, write formulas, or write final answers. The program validates every reference and computes the result deterministically.

variants.name: candidate_cell_ids_operation
variants.prompt_suffix: Return exactly one JSON object and no other text. Generate up to three ranked candidates; do not explain. Use only this schema: {"candidates":[{"cell_ids":["r1c2","r1c3"],"operation":"divide","unit":"percent"}]}. Each candidate must use existing numeric cell IDs in calculation order. For percentage of a total use divide [part,total] with unit percent. For growth/increase/decrease use percent_change [new,old] with unit percent. For average select every requested period. For annual interest use multiply [principal,rate]. For ratio use ratio [numerator,denominator] with unit times. Include alternatives when row, column, denominator, or operation is ambiguous. The program validates every candidate and calculates the selected answer deterministically.
